en: Pure coconut oil is a liquid in warm weather but solidifies into a white solid when the temperature drops below 24 degrees Celsius.
Adding vinegar to warm carabao milk causes a chemical change that curdles proteins to form solid kesong puti cheese.
Halo-halo is a heterogeneous mixture because you can easily see and separate its distinct solid ingredients like ube halaya and sweet beans.
Grinding soaked glutinous rice into galapong is a physical change because the rice changes shape but remains the exact same chemical substance.
Capiz shells are translucent materials that allow some light to pass through, making them ideal for traditional Philippine window panels.
The sour taste of sinigang comes from a solution where tamarind extract completely dissolves its acidic compounds into the boiling water.
Abaca plant fibers possess high tensile strength, making them an excellent natural material for manufacturing durable maritime ropes.
Lava erupting from Mayon Volcano is liquid melted rock that quickly cools and hardens into solid igneous rock.
Fermenting coconut sap into sukang paombong is a chemical change because sugars transform into a completely new substance called acetic acid.
Harvesting sea salt in Dasol relies on the physical change of evaporation, where the sun turns liquid seawater into invisible water vapor.
Bamboo is a highly renewable material with a hollow cylindrical structure that gives it an excellent strength-to-weight ratio for construction scaffolding.
Soy sauce used in chicken adobo is a homogeneous solution because the dissolved salt and fermented soybeans look completely uniform.
